content.original:
नमो अरिहंताणं नमो सिद्धाणं नमो आयरियाणं ।
नमो उवज्झायाणं नमो लोए सव्वसाहूणं ॥
content.transliteration: namo arihaṃtāṇaṃ namo siddhāṇaṃ namo āyariyāṇaṃ | namo uvajjhāyāṇaṃ namo loe savvasāhūṇaṃ ||
content.text: Obeisance to the Arihantas (conquerors); obeisance to the Siddhas (liberated souls); obeisance to the Acharyas (spiritual masters); obeisance to the Upadhyayas (teachers); obeisance to all the Sadhus (monks) in the world.

content.original:
एसो पंचनमुक्कारो सव्वपावप्पणासणो ।
मंगलाणं च सव्वेसिं पढमं हवइ मंगलं ॥
content.transliteration: eso paṃcanamukkāro savvapāvappaṇāsaṇo | maṃgalāṇaṃ ca savvesiṃ paḍhamaṃ havai maṃgalaṃ ||
content.text: This fivefold obeisance destroys all sins, and among all auspicious things it is the foremost auspicious blessing.

content.original: तेणं कालेणं तेणं समएणं समणे भगवं महावीरे विहरइ ।
content.transliteration: teṇaṃ kāleṇaṃ teṇaṃ samaeṇaṃ samaṇe bhagavaṃ mahāvīre viharai |
content.text: In that period, at that time, the Venerable Ascetic Mahavira lived and walked upon the earth, shedding the light of supreme liberation.

content.original: समणे भगवं महावीरे कासवगोत्तेणं, तस्स णं तओ नामधेज्जा एवं आहिज्जंति—तम्हा वद्धमाणो य समणो य महावीरो य ।
content.transliteration: samaṇe bhagavaṃ mahāvīre kāsavagotteṇaṃ, tassa ṇaṃ tao nāmadhejjā evaṃ āhijjaṃti—tamhā vaddhamāṇo ya samaṇo ya mahāvīro ya |
content.text: The Venerable Ascetic Mahavira belonged to the Kashyapa gotra. Three names were bestowed upon him: Vardhamana ('the prosperous'), Shramana ('the ascetic'), and Mahavira ('the great hero').

content.original: तओ णं सा तिसला खत्तियाणी चउद्दस महासुविणे पासित्ताणं पडिबुद्धा ।
content.transliteration: tao ṇaṃ sā tisalā khattiyāṇī cauddasa mahāsuviṇe pāsittāṇaṃ paḍibuddhā |
content.text: Then Queen Trishala, resting in peaceful repose, beheld the fourteen great auspicious dreams and awoke in profound joy.

content.original:
गय-वसह-सीह-अभिसेय-दाम-ससि-दिणयरं झसं कुंभं ।
पउमसर-सागर-विमाण-भवण-रयणोच्चयं सिहिं च ॥
content.transliteration: gaya-vasaha-sīha-abhiseya-dāma-sasi-diṇayaraṃ jhasaṃ kuṃbhaṃ | paumasara-sāgara-vimāṇa-bhavaṇa-rayaṇoccayaṃ sihiṃ ca ||
content.text: The fourteen dreams were: a magnificent elephant, an auspicious bull, a fearless lion, Goddess Lakshmi anointed by elephants, a fragrant flower garland, the radiant full moon, the golden sun, a divine celestial flag, a vase of golden water, a lotus lake, the milky ocean, a celestial aerial abode (vimana), a heap of precious jewels, and a smokeless blazing fire.

content.original: एए सुविणे पासित्ता देवी परमविम्हिता जाया ।
content.transliteration: ee suviṇe pāsittā devī paramavimhitā jāyā |
content.text: Having beheld these fourteen dreams, the Queen was filled with wonder, and the royal palace resounded with divine joy.

content.original: सिद्धत्थेणं खत्तिएणं सुविणपाढगा सद्दावेत्ता पुच्छिया ।
content.transliteration: siddhattheṇaṃ khattieṇaṃ suviṇapāḍhagā saddāvettā pucchiyā |
content.text: King Siddhartha summoned the interpreters of dreams and inquired into the spiritual significance of the fourteen auspicious visions.

content.original: महापुरिसो जइ भविस्सइ, तित्थंकरे वा चक्कवट्टी वा भविस्सइ ।
content.transliteration: mahāpuriso jai bhavissai, titthaṃkare vā cakkavaṭṭī vā bhavissai |
content.text: The interpreters replied: 'A supreme personage will be born! He will either become a Universal Sovereign (Chakravartin) or a supreme Tirthankara, establishing the ford across the ocean of worldly existence.'

content.original: तए णं समणे भगवं महावीरे नवण्हं मासाणं दसाण य राइंदियाणं विइकंताणं सुकुमालपाणिपाए जाओ ।
content.transliteration: tae ṇaṃ samaṇe bhagavaṃ mahāvīre navaṇhaṃ māsāṇaṃ dasāṇa ya rāiṃdiyāṇaṃ viikaṃtāṇaṃ sukumālapāṇipāe jāo |
content.text: After nine months and ten days, the Venerable Ascetic Mahavira was born, endowed with all auspicious marks and tender lotus-like limbs.

content.original: सकललोए आलोगो अहोसि, देवा देविंदा य महामहिमं करिसु ।
content.transliteration: sakalaloe ālogo ahosi, devā deviṃdā ya mahāmahimaṃ karisu |
content.text: A boundless spiritual light filled all the worlds, and the gods and Indras celebrated the grand birth festival (Janma Kalyanak) upon Mount Meru.

content.original: जाव जीवेण सह धम्मं पालइत्ता, तीसवत्थुसंमए संसारं परिच्चइत्ता दिक्खं पव्वइए ।
content.transliteration: jāva jīveṇa saha dhammaṃ pālaittā, tīsavatthusaṃmae saṃsāraṃ pariccaittā dikkhaṃ pavvaie |
content.text: Having lived thirty years as a prince, Mahavira renounced all worldly wealth, royal power, and palace splendors, and embraced the life of homeless asceticism (Diksha Kalyanak).

content.original: अचेलगो हुत्वा समणे भगवं महावीरे बारस संवच्छराणि अणुकंपाए परीसहे सहइ ।
content.transliteration: acelago hutvā samaṇe bhagavaṃ mahāvīre bārasa saṃvaccharāṇi aṇukaṃpāe parīsahe sahai |
content.text: Renouncing all possessions and garments, for twelve years the Venerable Mahavira endured severe hardships, insults, cold, heat, and physical perils with absolute equanimity.

content.original: सदा समाहितो अकुतोभयो, ध्यानेन अकलुषो विहरइ ।
content.transliteration: sadā samāhito akutobhayo, dhyānena akaluṣo viharai |
content.text: Ever meditative, fearless, compassionate, and pure in heart, he harbored no enmity toward any living being.

content.original: जुम्भियगामस्स बाहिरियाए उज्जुवालियाए णईए तीरे सालोरुक्खस्स अहे केवलज्ञानं उप्पन्नं ।
content.transliteration: jumbhiyagāmassa bāhiriyāe ujjuvāliyāe ṇaīe tīre sālorukkhassa ahe kevalajñānaṃ uppannaṃ |
content.text: Outside the town of Jrimbhikagrama, on the banks of the river Rijupalika, beneath a sala tree, supreme, infinite, unexcelled omniscience (Kevala Jnana) arose within Him.

content.original: सकलभावाणं जाणए पासए सव्वन्नू सव्वदरिसी जाओ ।
content.transliteration: sakalabhāvāṇaṃ jāṇae pāsae savvannū savvadarisī jāo |
content.text: He became omniscient, all-perceiving, knowing and seeing the thoughts, lives, and modifications of all beings across all time.

content.original: चउव्विहस्स संघस्स पण्णवेत्ता—समणा, समणीओ, सावया, साविगाओ ।
content.transliteration: cauvvihassa saṃghassa paṇṇavettā—samaṇā, samaṇīo, sāvayā, sāvigāo |
content.text: He established the fourfold holy congregation: monks (sadhus), nuns (sadhvis), laymen (shravakas), and laywomen (shravikas).

content.original: अहिंसासच्चअचौर्यब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहरूपं पंचमहाव्वयं उवदिसइ ।
content.transliteration: ahiṃsāsaccaacauryabrahmacaryāparigraharūpaṃ paṃcamahāvvayaṃ uvadisai |
content.text: He expounded the Five Great Vows: Non-violence (Ahimsa), Truthfulness (Satya), Non-stealing (Achaurya), Chastity (Brahmacharya), and Non-possessiveness (Aparigraha).

content.original: सव्वे पाणा न हंतव्वा, न परिघेत्तव्वा, न परितावेयव्वा ।
content.transliteration: savve pāṇā na haṃtavvā, na parighettavvā, na paritāveyavvā |
content.text: All living creatures, all beings, all souls should not be slain, nor treated with violence, nor abused, nor tormented, nor driven away.

content.original: इत्थं भगवया धम्मो देसिओ, बहुजणहिताय बहुजणसुहाय ।
content.transliteration: itthaṃ bhagavayā dhammo desio, bahujaṇahitāya bahujaṇasuhāya |
content.text: Thus was the Dharma expounded by the Blessed One, for the spiritual welfare of many, for the joy and liberation of all beings.

content.original: पावाए नयरीए हत्थिवालस्स रन्नो रज्जुसभाए समणे भगवं महावीरे कालगओ मुत्तो ।
content.transliteration: pāvāe nayarīe hatthivālassa ranno rajjusabhāe samaṇe bhagavaṃ mahāvīre kālagao mutto |
content.text: In the town of Pavapuri, in the assembly hall of King Hastipala, having delivered his final discourses, the Venerable Ascetic Mahavira attained final liberation (Nirvana Kalyanak).

content.original: सव्वदुक्खप्पहीणो सिद्धो बुद्धो परिनिव्वुडो जाव अंतं करेसि ।
content.transliteration: savvadukkhappahīṇo siddho buddho parinivvuḍo jāva aṃtaṃ karesi |
content.text: Freed from all suffering, perfected, enlightened, liberated, he put a complete and final end to the cycle of transmigration.

content.original: दिवंगए नाहे, देवा मणुया य दीवोत्सवेणं पूयं करिसु ।
content.transliteration: divaṃgae nāhe, devā maṇuyā ya dīvotsaveṇaṃ pūyaṃ karisu |
content.text: When the Supreme Master ascended to Nirvana, gods and humans illuminated the darkness with rows of earthen lamps, instituting the festival of Diwali.

content.original: पासस्स वि अरहओ पुरिसादाणीयरस बारस संवच्छराणि छउमत्थकालो अहोसि ।
content.transliteration: pāsassa vi arahao purisādāṇīyarasa bārasa saṃvaccharāṇi chaumatthakālo ahosi |
content.text: Likewise, Lord Parshvanatha, the revered 23rd Tirthankara, attained Kevala Jnana after profound meditation and guided humanity on the path of non-violence.

content.original: कप्पसुत्तमिणं सुयं पठित्ता सुणित्ता य, जीवा संसारसागरं तरंति ।
content.transliteration: kappasuttamiṇaṃ suyaṃ paṭhittā suṇittā ya, jīvā saṃsārasāgaraṃ taraṃti |
content.text: Having heard, recited, and contemplated this sacred Kalpa Sutra, living souls safely cross the vast and perilous ocean of worldly existence.
